body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep progress reports off the Lead dispatch path**

When a Worker uses `report.state = 'progress'`, the handler only validates blocked reports here and still sends every call through `dispatchOrcaToolMessage` with `message`; this can start an idle Lead turn or queue an internal progress note while busy. Because `captureLocalWorkerReport` leaves the assignment pending for progress, a Worker that then ends without another settling report is also text-auto-bridged, so the Lead gets progress plus final text rather than an internal update. Handle progress as a storage-only update and skip dispatch.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace stale report state when a Worker returns to waiting**

After a prior blocked or failed report, a later waiting report is captured in runtime state, but this branch calls only `markWorkerIdle`; the store implementation updates status and idle time without replacing `latest_report`. The broadcast then leaves the previous awaiting-answer chip in place, and `findOrcaWorkerReportQuestion` can attach the obsolete question to a later error notification. Persist the waiting report or clear the old one here.

If a Lead steers a replacement assignment while a Worker is in the progress path, `recordWorkerReport` captures the old `AutoBridgeState`, awaits `getWorkerLinkBySessionId`, and then writes without checking that the state is still current; `dispatchResolvedWorker` can replace the assignment and clear `latest_report` during that await. Recheck the assignment identity under the worker transition before persisting.

When a Worker records `progress` and its final `send_to_lead` callback settles after the terminal event, this case lets the terminal handler apply progress and set `reportApplied`. The late callback then skips both state mapping and report persistence, so a final `waiting` can remain `done` and final `blocked`, `failed`, or `dropped` reports never update their chip or attention state.
